ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A number of linked rings, each 1 cm thick, are hanging on a peg. The top ring has an outside diameter of 20 cm. The outside diameter of each of the outer rings is 1 cm less than that of the ring above it. The bottom ring has an outside diameter of 3 cm. What is the distance, in cm, from the top of the top ring to the bottom of the bottom ring?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a string of interlocked rings up and down, forming a vertically hanging chain. Beside the topmost ring, the outer diameter is marked as 20 cm; the inner opening height of the same ring is marked as 18 cm, so the outer diameter and inner diameter differ by 2 cm, corresponding to a ring thickness of 1 cm. In the figure, adjacent rings pass through each other, so each pair of adjacent rings has overlap in the vertical direction. Reasoning: The outer diameters of the rings in order are 20, 19, 18, ..., 3. This arithmetic sequence has 20 - 3 + 1 = 18 rings in total. If the overlap caused by interlocking is not considered, the sum of the vertical lengths of all ring outer diameters is (20 + 3) × 18 / 2 = 207 cm. Each two adjacent interlocked rings overlap by 2 cm, namely one 1 cm ring thickness on the upper and lower sides respectively; among 18 rings there are 17 adjacent connections, so the total overlap is 17 × 2 = 34 cm. Therefore the distance from the top of the topmost ring to the bottom of the bottommost ring is 207 - 34 = 173 cm.

method.method_draft: Use a total-diameters-minus-overlaps model. From the image, note that the rings form a vertical linked chain and that the top ring’s outer diameter is labeled 20 while its inner opening is labeled 18, confirming that a 1 cm thick ring loses 2 cm between outside and inside diameter. From the text, list the outside diameters as 20, 19, 18, ..., 3, so there are 18 rings. If the rings were simply stacked without interlinking, their vertical sizes would sum to the arithmetic-series total. But each adjacent linked pair overlaps vertically by 2 cm, one ring-thickness at the top and one at the bottom, as indicated by the annular linking in the image. Compute sum(20 through 3) = 207, subtract 2 cm for each of the 17 links: 207 - 34 = 173.

method.method_draft: Use an incremental inner-diameter contribution model. From the image, first observe that after the top ring, each next ring hangs through the previous ring’s opening; the labeled 20 outside and 18 inside on the top ring illustrate that a ring of outside diameter D has inner diameter D - 2. From the text, the ring diameters are 20, 19, 18, ..., 3. The full height begins with the entire top ring, 20 cm. Each lower ring adds only the distance from where it passes through the previous ring down to its own bottom, which equals its inner diameter, D - 2. Therefore add 20 plus the inner diameters of the remaining rings: (19 - 2), (18 - 2), ..., (3 - 2), i.e. 20 + 17 + 16 + ... + 1 = 20 + 153 = 173.
